# **Utsav MasterPrint: Autonomous Engineering Specification for Project Utsav**

## **Executive Summary and Architectural Paradigm**

Project Utsav is an agentic, reactive celebration and event planning command center engineered for weddings, birthdays, and community events. Traditional event management suffers from severe operational fragmentation across disconnected spreadsheets, messaging groups, and static inspiration boards, while early generative artificial intelligence wrappers merely output uneditable walls of Markdown text. When real-world constraints shift—such as an unexpected guest count increase or a higher-than-estimated catering quote—static text outputs become obsolete, forcing event hosts to regenerate plans from scratch and lose tracked progress.  
Utsav resolves this multi-constraint state management problem by treating event planning as a synchronized, single-source-of-truth JSON state tree powered by Google's @google/genai SDK and structured outputs1. Designed specifically for autonomous implementation within Google Antigravity—Google's agent-first development platform where multiple autonomous agents execute task planning, file navigation, terminal CLI operations (agy), and live browser verification in parallel4—this MasterPrint provides the complete functional, structural, and programmatic blueprint required to compile and launch the application.  
In the runtime architecture, the user interface layer is cleanly decoupled from the external artificial intelligence service module (src/services/geminiService.ts), which acts as the sole integration point with Google's Gemini API3. This separation ensures that client-side state transitions—such as toggling a vendor task checkbox, switching local map categories, or locking a specific venue quote—occur instantaneously in the browser, whereas structural recalculations invoke targeted, schema-constrained model completions1. During multi-turn plan adjustments, the orchestration layer employs a sliding window of the last 10 conversation turns prefixed with role identities to maintain conversational coherence without risking context window overflow3.  
Beyond technical reactivity, Utsav introduces a fundamental psychological shift in human-AI interaction. Event hosts frequently experience decision fatigue and budget anxiety. Rather than exposing crisis-oriented interfaces that amplify host tension, Utsav embeds a proactive **Peace-of-Mind Shield** into the initial calculation engine and pairs it with **Utsav Sahayak**, a calm co-planner bar. Every generated plan automatically reserves a 10% financial comfort cushion, injects a 10% extra plate buffer into catering briefs, and pre-populates weather and power backup verifications into the venue checklist. When preferences or guest counts evolve, Utsav Sahayak smoothly recalibrates unlocked budget categories, menu formats, and run-of-show timelines while preserving all previously checked vendor tasks and user customizations.

## **Functional Pillars and User Experience Specification**

Project Utsav replaces conversational guesswork with a deterministic, four-stage operational pipeline that guides hosts from initial conceptualization to event-day execution.

### **Calm Four-Step Onboarding Intake and Demo Presets**

Instead of confronting the host with an empty text prompt, the application launches with a structured, low-friction intake wizard (src/components/OnboardingIntake.tsx) that captures four foundational constraints in sequence. First, the host selects the **Event Archetype and Sub-Event**, choosing among a Wedding (with multi-function support for Haldi, Mehendi, Sangeet, Wedding Ceremony, and Reception), a Birthday Celebration (Milestone, Kids Theme, or Intimate Dinner), or a Community Event (College Cultural Fest, Hackathon, Housing Society Festival, or Charity Fundraiser). Second, the host establishes the **Geographic Anchor and Venue Setting** by entering the target city and neighborhood or PIN code—which simultaneously calibrates regional vendor pricing tiers and anchors the embedded local vendor map—alongside the venue setting preference (Indoor Banquet, Outdoor Lawn, Rooftop/Terrace, or Community Hall/Campus). Third, the host configures **Guest Capacity and Target Date** via an interactive numeric stepper for guest count (![][image1]) and a calendar picker that computes the days remaining until the celebration (![][image2]). Fourth, the host adjusts the **Total Budget and Regional Culinary Vibe**, utilizing a budget slider denominated in Indian Rupees (from ₹10,000 to ₹50,00,000+) paired with selectable **Regional Culinary Vibe Cards**, dietary preferences, and aesthetic tags such as *Eco-Friendly & Zero Plastic*, *Marigold & Brass Heritage*, or *Minimalist Pastel & Fairy Lights*.  
To guarantee frictionless evaluation during live demonstrations and judging, the top of the intake module integrates three instant preview presets that populate the entire intake state in a single click:

| Preset Identifier | Event Archetype & Name | Guest Capacity | Total Budget (INR) | Regional Culinary Trigger & Setting |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| preset\_wedding | **Royal Jaipur Sangeet & Wedding** (Wedding) | 150 Guests | ₹8,00,000 | **Northern Naan & Nawabi** • Outdoor Lawn |
| preset\_birthday | **1st Milestone Birthday Garden Soiree** (Birthday) | 80 Guests | ₹65,000 | **Southern Sambar & Sadhya** • Rooftop / Terrace |
| preset\_community | **Campus Cultural & Tech Utsav** (Community) | 350 Guests | ₹2,50,000 | **Global Fusion & Street** • Community Hall / Campus |

### **The Proactive Peace-of-Mind Shield**

Immediately upon generating the master plan, Utsav renders a persistent, calming emerald banner (src/components/PeaceOfMindBanner.tsx) across the top of the command center. This module eliminates host anxiety by proving that operational buffers are already baked into the quantitative foundation of the event. Specifically, the calculation engine automatically deducts 10% of the total budget (![][image3]) into a protected reserve before distributing funds across active vendor categories:  
![][image4]  
![][image5]  
Simultaneously, the catering engine configures the vendor brief for ![][image6] plates so food never runs short, while anchoring the per-plate target to the allocated catering budget:  
![][image7]  
Finally, the shield pre-populates high-priority verification tasks into the logistics timeline for weather contingency (such as a covered backup pavilion for outdoor lawns), generator power backup, acoustic licensing, and fire safety compliance.

Supports inline actual-spend logging and **Category Lock toggles**. | Computes live variance (![][image8]), per-guest cost (![][image9]), and passes locked category flags (isLocked: boolean) to Utsav Sahayak during rebalancing. |

### **Regional Culinary Triggers Specification**

In Indian celebrations, catering routinely represents 35% to 50% of total event expenditure. Generic AI planners fail hosts by suggesting generic menu placeholders disconnected from regional culture and per-plate economics. Project Utsav governs menu synthesis through four structured culinary triggers that adapt dynamically to the calculated per-plate budget (![][image10]):

| Culinary Trigger ID | Display Title | Signature Culinary Elements & Live Stations | Ideal Event Archetype Match |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| southern\_sambar | **Southern Sambar & Sadhya** | Mini-tiffin podi idli counters, Ghee Roast & Appam live stations, traditional banana-leaf Sadhya spreads, Avial, Malabar Parotta with vegetable stew, Elaneer Payasam, and Brass-Davara Filter Coffee bars. | South Indian Weddings, Upanayanam, Society Harvest Festivals, Morning Receptions. |
| northern\_naan | **Northern Naan & Nawabi** | Old-Delhi Chaat street carts (Palak Patta Chaat, Dahi Bhalla), Amritsari Kulcha & Bhatti Paneer tandoors, slow-cooked Dal Makhani, Peshawari Naan baskets, Jalebi-Rabri live wok, and Kulfi Falooda carts. | Sangeet Nights, North Indian Winter Weddings, Milestone Anniversaries, Diwali Melas. |
| deccan\_nizami | **Deccan & Royal Nizami** | Dum Biryani handis (Veg Subz & Zafrani), Pathar-ka-Gosht / Paneer Shikampuri grills, Mirchi ka Salan, Baghara Baingan, Double ka Meetha, Qubani ka Meetha, and Irani Chai with Osmania biscuits. | Evening Receptions, Grand Community Gatherings, Royal Heritage Theme Events. |
| global\_fusion | **Global Fusion & Street** | Wood-fired Neapolitan pizza ovens, gourmet sliders, Mexican taco & nacho bars, Peri-Peri fries, artisanal pasta tossed in cheese wheels, and DIY Boba Tea & botanical mocktail stations. | Birthday Parties, College Cultural Fests, Hackathons, Youth Meetups, Cocktail Evenings. |

### **Utsav Sahayak: The Calm Co-Planner Bar**

Positioned as a floating dock at the bottom of the viewport (src/components/UtsavSahayakBar.tsx), **Utsav Sahayak** replaces stressful crisis terminology with reassuring, human-centric guidance. Hosts can either enter natural language adjustments or trigger four pre-engineered calm adjustment workflows:

| Quick-Action Chip Label | State Override Triggered | Underlying AI Rebalancing Mechanism |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **✨ Welcome \+25 more guests within budget** | guestCount: current \+ 25 | Holds totalBudgetINR and locked categories constant while shifting high-cost plated items toward high-yield live stations and updating seating counts. |
| **🌿 Make decor & flow 15% more budget-cosy** | totalBudgetINR: current \* 0.85 | Recommends graceful aesthetic swaps (such as replacing imported floral stages with local marigold drapes, brass diyas, and warm fairy lighting) without hurting food quality. |
| **🏡 Adapt outdoor plan to cosy indoor flow** | venueType: 'Indoor Banquet' | Reallocates outdoor weather-proofing and tenting reserves toward indoor acoustic styling, stage drapery, and warm ambient lighting. |
| **🍛 Switch or blend Regional Feast Palate** | Cycles regionalVibe or blends live counters | Rewrites feastMenu to match the newly selected regional palate while strictly honoring the existing perPlateBudgetINR ceiling. |

## **Antigravity Agentic Execution Strategy and Technology Stack**

Google Antigravity functions as an autonomous multi-agent development environment across its desktop IDE, browser integration, and terminal CLI (agy)4. Rather than acting as a single-threaded autocomplete tool, Antigravity coordinates specialized agents that perform task planning, step-by-step execution, accurate file navigation, and automated walkthrough verification simultaneously4. To ensure zero friction during Antigravity's autonomous build and verification cycles, Project Utsav utilizes a self-contained React 19, TypeScript, and Vite stack backed by localStorage state persistence and the official @google/genai SDK3.  
![][image15]

### **Mandatory SDK Selection and Schema Governance**

A foundational requirement for the Antigravity build process is the exclusive adoption of the modern @google/genai TypeScript SDK (v2.30.0+), strictly avoiding the legacy @google/generative-ai (v0.24.x) package10. Whereas the legacy library required instantiating GenerativeModel objects directly, @google/genai standardizes all operations through a unified GoogleGenAI client instance invoking ai.models.generateContent or ai.models.generateContentStream11.  
Furthermore, Google Gemini's structured output engine exhibits distinct architectural advantages and constraints compared to competing LLM providers1. Unlike OpenAI, which requires every property to be listed in required with additionalProperties: false and forces optional properties into union type arrays, or Anthropic, which rejects numeric bounds (minimum, maximum) and caps nullable union parameters at 16 across a request, Gemini natively supports numeric bounds, item count constraints (minItems, maxItems), and nullable: true flags without schema-modifying boilerplate1. However, setting responseMimeType: "application/json" alone in a Gemini request acts only as a strong hint and carries a small risk of generating malformed JSON syntax1. To guarantee 100% valid, type-safe JSON objects, requests in Utsav must supply both responseMimeType: "application/json" and a strict responseSchema (constructed via the Type enum from @google/genai) or responseJsonSchema (constructed via z.toJSONSchema() in Zod)1.  
Because the size of a responseSchema counts directly toward the input token limit and overly intricate schemas can trigger an HTTP InvalidArgument: 400 error, the Utsav schema architecture enforces strict structural discipline1. Property identifiers and enum literals are kept concise, nested object arrays are flattened to a maximum depth of two levels, optional properties are minimized in favor of required deterministic fields, and client-side JSON validation is paired with an automatic retry wrapper1. Equally important, system prompts in geminiService.ts never duplicate the schema definition or embed raw JSON examples in the prompt text, as duplicating the schema in both the config object and the prompt degrades model output quality1.

### **Terminal Installation Commands for Antigravity CLI (agy)**

The Antigravity terminal agent shall execute the following initialization sequence in the project root directory5:

Bash  
\# 1\. Scaffold Vite \+ React \+ TypeScript project in current directory  
npm create vite@latest . \-- \--template react-ts

\# 2\. Install core runtime dependencies including official @google/genai SDK  
npm install @google/genai zod lucide-react canvas-confetti

\# 3\. Install development and styling dependencies  
npm install \-D tailwindcss@3 postcss autoprefixer @types/canvas-confetti

\# 4\. Initialize Tailwind CSS configuration  
npx tailwindcss init \-p

## **Core Data Contracts and Unified State Schema (src/types/utsav.ts)**

Every component in Project Utsav reads from and writes to a unified TypeScript interface (UtsavEventState). By keeping the data contract flat and strictly typed, the exact same schema powers initial rendering, local user edits, and reactive AI rebalancing1.  
Antigravity shall create src/types/utsav.ts with the following specification:

TypeScript  
export type EventCategory \= 'Wedding' | 'Birthday' | 'Community';

export type RegionalVibeId \=  
  | 'southern\_sambar'  
  | 'northern\_naan'  
  | 'deccan\_nizami'  
  | 'global\_fusion';

export interface EventIntake {  
  eventName: string;  
  category: EventCategory;  
  subEvent: string;  
  city: string;  
  venueType: 'Indoor Banquet' | 'Outdoor Lawn' | 'Rooftop / Terrace' | 'Community Hall / Campus';  
  eventDate: string;  
  guestCount: number;  
  totalBudgetINR: number;  
  regionalVibe: RegionalVibeId;  
  dietaryPreference: 'Pure Veg' | 'Veg & Non-Veg' | 'Jain & Veg Friendly' | 'Vegan Options';  
  aestheticTags: string\[\];  
}

export interface BudgetAllocationItem {  
  id: string;  
  categoryName: string;  
  percentage: number;  
  allocatedINR: number;  
  actualSpentINR: number;  
  isLocked: boolean;  
  notes: string;  
}

export interface FeastMenu {  
  regionalTitle: string;  
  perPlateBudgetINR: number;  
  cateredPlateCount: number; // Includes \+10% Peace-of-Mind plate buffer  
  welcomeDrinks: string\[\];  
  startersAndLiveCounters: string\[\];  
  mainCourseSpecialties: string\[\];  
  breadsAndRice: string\[\];  
  desserts: string\[\];  
  catererQuantityBrief: string;  
}

export interface ThemeConcept {  
  id: string;  
  themeName: string;  
  vibeDescription: string;  
  colorPaletteHex: string\[\]; // Array of 4 hex strings e.g. \["\#D97706", "\#7C2D12", "\#FEF3C7", "\#065F46"\]  
  decorFocalPoints: string\[\];  
  engagementActivities: string\[\];  
  digitalInviteCopy: string;  
}

export interface TimelineItem {  
  id: string;  
  phase: 'Pre-Event Countdown' | 'Event-Day Run Sheet';  
  timeMarker: string; // e.g., "T-30 Days" or "06:30 PM"  
  taskTitle: string;  
  assignedRole: string;  
  completed: boolean;  
  isSafetyCheck: boolean;  
}

export interface VendorItem {  
  id: string;  
  serviceCategory: 'Caterers' | 'Decorators' | 'Photographers' | 'Venues' | 'Sound & Artist';  
  taskTitle: string;  
  estimatedPriceRangeINR: string;  
  vettingQuestions: string\[\];  
  whatsappInquiryTemplate: string;  
  pinnedVendorName: string;  
  quotedPriceINR: number;  
  booked: boolean;  
}

export interface PeaceOfMindShield {  
  comfortCushionINR: number;  
  extraPlateBufferCount: number;  
  weatherAndPowerSafeguard: string;  
  calmReassuranceNote: string;  
}

export interface SahayakMessage {  
  id: string;  
  role: 'user' | 'model';  
  senderTag: 'Host' | 'UtsavSahayak';  
  text: string;  
  timestamp: string;  
}

export interface UtsavEventState {  
  intake: EventIntake;  
  peaceOfMind: PeaceOfMindShield;  
  costPerGuestINR: number;  
  budgetBreakdown: BudgetAllocationItem\[\];  
  feastMenu: FeastMenu;  
  themeConcepts: ThemeConcept\[\];  
  selectedThemeIndex: number;  
  timeline: TimelineItem\[\];  
  vendors: VendorItem\[\];  
  sahayakHistory: SahayakMessage\[\];  
  lastSahayakSummary: string;  
}

## **Gemini API Integration and Structured Output Service (src/services/geminiService.ts)**

The src/services/geminiService.ts module handles all communication with Google's Gemini API3. It initializes a reusable GoogleGenAI client instance using import.meta.env.VITE\_GEMINI\_API\_KEY and executes structured JSON generation via ai.models.generateContent against gemini-2.5-flash3.  
Within this service, UTSAV\_PLAN\_SCHEMA uses the Type enumeration from @google/genai (Type.OBJECT, Type.ARRAY, Type.STRING, Type.NUMBER, Type.BOOLEAN) to guarantee syntactically valid JSON responses1. During reactive adjustments via rebalanceWithSahayak(), the service formats the most recent 10 turns from sahayakHistory using role prefixes (\[Host\]: and \[UtsavSahayak\]:)3 and merges the newly generated plan with existing client state so that locked budget categories (isLocked: true), checked timeline milestones (completed: true), and booked vendor records (booked: true, pinnedVendorName, quotedPriceINR) are preserved across recalculations.  
Antigravity shall create src/services/geminiService.ts with the following implementation:

TypeScript  
import { GoogleGenAI, Type, Schema } from '@google/genai';  
import {  
  EventIntake,  
  UtsavEventState,  
  SahayakMessage  
} from '../types/utsav';  
import { REGIONAL\_VIBES } from '../constants/regionalVibes';

const apiKey \= import.meta.env.VITE\_GEMINI\_API\_KEY || '';  
const ai \= new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey });

const MODEL\_NAME \= 'gemini-2.5-flash';

const UTSAV\_PLAN\_SCHEMA: Schema \= {  
  type: Type.OBJECT,  
  properties: {  
    peaceOfMind: {  
      type: Type.OBJECT,  
      properties: {  
        comfortCushionINR: { type: Type.NUMBER },  
        extraPlateBufferCount: { type: Type.NUMBER },  
        weatherAndPowerSafeguard: { type: Type.STRING },  
        calmReassuranceNote: { type: Type.STRING }  
      },  
      required: \[  
        'comfortCushionINR',  
        'extraPlateBufferCount',  
        'weatherAndPowerSafeguard',  
        'calmReassuranceNote'  
      \]  
    },  
    costPerGuestINR: { type: Type.NUMBER },  
    budgetBreakdown: {  
      type: Type.ARRAY,  
      items: {  
        type: Type.OBJECT,  
        properties: {  
          id: { type: Type.STRING },  
          categoryName: { type: Type.STRING },  
          percentage: { type: Type.NUMBER },  
          allocatedINR: { type: Type.NUMBER },  
          notes: { type: Type.STRING }  
        },  
        required: \['id', 'categoryName', 'percentage', 'allocatedINR', 'notes'\]  
      }  
    },  
    feastMenu: {  
      type: Type.OBJECT,  
      properties: {  
        regionalTitle: { type: Type.STRING },  
        perPlateBudgetINR: { type: Type.NUMBER },  
        cateredPlateCount: { type: Type.NUMBER },  
        welcomeDrinks: { type: Type.ARRAY, items: { type: Type.STRING } },  
        startersAndLiveCounters: { type: Type.ARRAY, items: { type: Type.STRING } },  
        mainCourseSpecialties: { type: Type.ARRAY, items: { type: Type.STRING } },  
        breadsAndRice: { type: Type.ARRAY, items: { type: Type.STRING } },  
        desserts: { type: Type.ARRAY, items: { type: Type.STRING } },  
        catererQuantityBrief: { type: Type.STRING }  
      },  
      required: \[  
        'regionalTitle',  
        'perPlateBudgetINR',  
        'cateredPlateCount',  
        'welcomeDrinks',  
        'startersAndLiveCounters',  
        'mainCourseSpecialties',  
        'breadsAndRice',  
        'desserts',  
        'catererQuantityBrief'  
      \]  
    },  
    themeConcepts: {  
      type: Type.ARRAY,  
      items: {  
        type: Type.OBJECT,  
        properties: {  
          id: { type: Type.STRING },  
          themeName: { type: Type.STRING },  
          vibeDescription: { type: Type.STRING },  
          colorPaletteHex: { type: Type.ARRAY, items: { type: Type.STRING } },  
          decorFocalPoints: { type: Type.ARRAY, items: { type: Type.STRING } },  
          engagementActivities: { type: Type.ARRAY, items: { type: Type.STRING } },  
          digitalInviteCopy: { type: Type.STRING }  
        },  
        required: \[  
          'id',  
          'themeName',  
          'vibeDescription',  
          'colorPaletteHex',  
          'decorFocalPoints',  
          'engagementActivities',  
          'digitalInviteCopy'  
        \]  
      }  
    },  
    timeline: {  
      type: Type.ARRAY,  
      items: {  
        type: Type.OBJECT,  
        properties: {  
          id: { type: Type.STRING },  
          phase: {  
            type: Type.STRING,  
            enum: \['Pre-Event Countdown', 'Event-Day Run Sheet'\]  
          },  
          timeMarker: { type: Type.STRING },  
          taskTitle: { type: Type.STRING },  
          assignedRole: { type: Type.STRING },

        },

        \]  
      }  
    },

              'Caterers',

};

function formatSlidingWindowHistory(history: SahayakMessage\[\]): string {  
  const recentTurns \= history.slice(-10);  
  if (recentTurns.length \=== 0) return 'No prior adjustments.';  
  return recentTurns  
    .map((msg) \=\> \`\[\${msg.senderTag}\]: \${msg.text}\`)  
    .join('\\n');  
}

const SYSTEM\_INSTRUCTION\_MASTER \= \`  
Act as Utsav Sahayak, an empathetic, culturally grounded Indian celebration and event architect.  
Follow the provided responseSchema strictly.  
Core Operational Rules:  
1\. Always set aside exactly 10% of totalBudgetINR as the '10% Comfort Cushion (Peace-of-Mind Buffer)' inside budgetBreakdown and peaceOfMind.comfortCushionINR.  
2\. The sum of all allocatedINR across budgetBreakdown items must equal totalBudgetINR.  
3\. Calculate cateredPlateCount as Math.ceil(guestCount \* 1.10) so the event never runs short of food.  
4\. Calculate perPlateBudgetINR by dividing the Catering category's allocatedINR by cateredPlateCount.  
5\. Design feastMenu specifically around the chosen regionalVibe (Southern Sambar & Sadhya, Northern Naan & Nawabi, Deccan & Royal Nizami, or Global Fusion & Street) and ensure dishes realistically match the perPlateBudgetINR tier and dietaryPreference.  
6\. Provide exactly 3 distinct themeConcepts, each with 4 valid 6-digit CSS hex color codes (e.g. \#D97706), practical decor focal points, interactive guest games/activities, and a warm, ready-to-send digital invite message.  
7\. Provide at least 5 'Pre-Event Countdown' timeline tasks and 5 'Event-Day Run Sheet' minute-by-minute tasks, including proactive weather and power backup safety checks.  
8\. Provide actionable vendor items covering Caterers, Decorators, Photographers, Venues, and Sound & Artist with realistic price ranges in INR for the specified city, 3 practical vetting questions each, and a polite WhatsApp inquiry draft.  
9\. Maintain a calm, reassuring, warm tone in calmReassuranceNote and lastSahayakSummary that eliminates host stress.  
\`;

export async function generateInitialUtsavPlan(  
  intake: EventIntake  
): Promise\<UtsavEventState\> {  
  const regionalMeta \= REGIONAL\_VIBES\[intake.regionalVibe\];  
  const prompt \= \`  
Create a complete Utsav celebration master plan for:  
\- Event Name: \${intake.eventName}  
\- Category: \${intake.category} (\${intake.subEvent})  
\- Location: \${intake.city} | Venue Setting: \${intake.venueType}  
\- Date: \${intake.eventDate} | Guest Count: \${intake.guestCount}  
\- Total Budget: ₹\${intake.totalBudgetINR.toLocaleString('en-IN')}  
\- Regional Culinary Trigger: \${regionalMeta.title} (\${regionalMeta.tagline})  
\- Dietary Preference: \${intake.dietaryPreference}  
\- Aesthetic Vibes: \${intake.aestheticTags.join(', ')}  
\`;

  let attempt \= 0;  
  while (attempt \< 2) {  
    try {  
      const response \= await ai.models.generateContent({  
        model: MODEL\_NAME,  
        contents: prompt,  
        config: {  
          systemInstruction: SYSTEM\_INSTRUCTION\_MASTER,  
          responseMimeType: 'application/json',  
          responseSchema: UTSAV\_PLAN\_SCHEMA,  
          temperature: 0.4  
        }  
      });

      const rawText \= response.text || '{}';  
      const parsed \= JSON.parse(rawText);

      return hydrateFullState(intake, parsed);  
    } catch (error) {  
      attempt \+= 1;  
      console.error(\`Utsav synthesis attempt \${attempt} failed:\`, error);  
      if (attempt \>= 2) {  
        throw new Error(  
          'Utsav Sahayak encountered a temporary connection pause. Verify VITE\_GEMINI\_API\_KEY and retry.'  
        );  
      }  
    }  
  }  
  throw new Error('Unexpected synthesis termination.');  
}

export async function rebalanceWithSahayak(  
  currentState: UtsavEventState,  
  userRequest: string,  
  updatedIntakeOverrides?: Partial\<EventIntake\>  
): Promise\<UtsavEventState\> {  
  const mergedIntake: EventIntake \= {  
    ...currentState.intake,  
    ...updatedIntakeOverrides  
  };

  const lockedCategories \= currentState.budgetBreakdown  
    .filter((b) \=\> b.isLocked)  
    .map((b) \=\> \`\${b.categoryName}: Locked at ₹\${b.allocatedINR}\`)  
    .join(', ');

  const slidingHistoryText \= formatSlidingWindowHistory(  
    currentState.sahayakHistory  
  );

  const prompt \= \`  
Current Event Parameters:  
\- Event: \${mergedIntake.eventName} (\${mergedIntake.category} \- \${mergedIntake.subEvent})  
\- City: \${mergedIntake.city} | Setting: \${mergedIntake.venueType}  
\- Guest Count: \${mergedIntake.guestCount} | Total Budget: ₹\${mergedIntake.totalBudgetINR}  
\- Regional Culinary Trigger: \${REGIONAL\_VIBES\[mergedIntake.regionalVibe\].title}  
\- Dietary: \${mergedIntake.dietaryPreference}  
\- Locked Budget Categories (DO NOT alter allocatedINR for these): \${lockedCategories || 'None'}

Recent Conversation Window:  
\${slidingHistoryText}

Latest Host Adjustment Request:  
"\${userRequest}"

Smoothly rebalance the budgetBreakdown, feastMenu, themeConcepts, timeline, and vendors to honor the request and any locked categories while keeping the host completely stress-free. Explain the graceful adjustments in lastSahayakSummary.  
\`;

  const response \= await ai.models.generateContent({  
    model: MODEL\_NAME,  
    contents: prompt,  
    config: {  
      systemInstruction: SYSTEM\_INSTRUCTION\_MASTER,  
      responseMimeType: 'application/json',  
      responseSchema: UTSAV\_PLAN\_SCHEMA,  
      temperature: 0.35  
    }  
  });

  const parsed \= JSON.parse(response.text || '{}');  
  const nextState \= hydrateFullState(mergedIntake, parsed, currentState);

  const now \= new Date().toLocaleTimeString(\[\], {  
    hour: '2-digit',  
    minute: '2-digit'  
  });

  nextState.sahayakHistory \= \[  
    ...currentState.sahayakHistory.slice(-8),  
    {  
      id: \`usr-\${Date.now()}\`,  
      role: 'user',  
      senderTag: 'Host',  
      text: userRequest,  
      timestamp: now  
    },  
    {  
      id: \`mdl-\${Date.now() \+ 1}\`,  
      role: 'model',  
      senderTag: 'UtsavSahayak',  
      text: parsed.lastSahayakSummary || 'Plan smoothly recalibrated.',  
      timestamp: now  
    }  
  \];

  return nextState;  
}

function hydrateFullState(  
  intake: EventIntake,  
  rawModelData: any,  
  previousState?: UtsavEventState  
): UtsavEventState {  
  const prevBudgetMap \= new Map(  
    previousState?.budgetBreakdown.map((b) \=\> \[b.categoryName, b\]) || \[\]  
  );  
  const prevTimelineMap \= new Map(  
    previousState?.timeline.map((t) \=\> \[t.taskTitle, t\]) || \[\]  
  );  
  const prevVendorMap \= new Map(  
    previousState?.vendors.map((v) \=\> \[v.serviceCategory, v\]) || \[\]  
  );

  return {  
    intake,  
    peaceOfMind: rawModelData.peaceOfMind,  
    costPerGuestINR:  
      rawModelData.costPerGuestINR ||  
      Math.round(intake.totalBudgetINR / Math.max(1, intake.guestCount)),  
    budgetBreakdown: (rawModelData.budgetBreakdown || \[\]).map(  
      (item: any, idx: number) \=\> {  
        const existing \= prevBudgetMap.get(item.categoryName);  
        return {  
          id: item.id || \`b-\${idx}\`,  
          categoryName: item.categoryName,  
          percentage: item.percentage,  
          allocatedINR: existing?.isLocked  
            ? existing.allocatedINR  
            : item.allocatedINR,  
          actualSpentINR: existing?.actualSpentINR || 0,  
          isLocked: existing?.isLocked || false,  
          notes: item.notes  
        };  
      }  
    ),  
    feastMenu: rawModelData.feastMenu,  
    themeConcepts: rawModelData.themeConcepts || \[\],  
    selectedThemeIndex: previousState?.selectedThemeIndex || 0,  
    timeline: (rawModelData.timeline || \[\]).map((item: any, idx: number) \=\> {  
      const existing \= prevTimelineMap.get(item.taskTitle);  
      return {  
        id: item.id || \`t-\${idx}\`,  
        phase: item.phase,  
        timeMarker: item.timeMarker,  
        taskTitle: item.taskTitle,  
        assignedRole: item.assignedRole,  
        completed: existing?.completed || false,  
        isSafetyCheck: Boolean(item.isSafetyCheck)  
      };  
    }),  
    vendors: (rawModelData.vendors || \[\]).map((item: any, idx: number) \=\> {  
      const existing \= prevVendorMap.get(item.serviceCategory);  
      return {  
        id: item.id || \`v-\${idx}\`,  
        serviceCategory: item.serviceCategory,  
        taskTitle: item.taskTitle,  
        estimatedPriceRangeINR: item.estimatedPriceRangeINR,  
        vettingQuestions: item.vettingQuestions || \[\],  
        whatsappInquiryTemplate: item.whatsappInquiryTemplate,  
        pinnedVendorName: existing?.pinnedVendorName || '',  
        quotedPriceINR: existing?.quotedPriceINR || 0,  
        booked: existing?.booked || false  
      };  
    }),  
    sahayakHistory: previousState?.sahayakHistory || \[\],  
    lastSahayakSummary:  
      rawModelData.lastSahayakSummary ||  
      'Initial Utsav plan crafted with a 10% Comfort Cushion and \+10% extra catering buffer.'  
  };  
}

## **Component-Level Architecture and Implementation Specifications**

### **WhatsApp Vendor Brief Generator (src/utils/whatsappHelper.ts)**

To turn static vendor checklists into immediate execution tools, src/utils/whatsappHelper.ts constructs an actionable WhatsApp outreach payload that pre-fills the event date, city, guest count, budget expectation, and the three generated vetting questions:

TypeScript  
import { EventIntake, VendorItem } from '../types/utsav';

export function buildVendorWhatsAppMessage(  
  intake: EventIntake,  
  vendor: VendorItem  
): string {  
  const greeting \= \`Namaste\! Reaching out regarding the upcoming \${intake.eventName} (\${intake.category} \- \${intake.subEvent}).\`;  
  const specs \= \`\\n📅 Date: \${intake.eventDate}\\n📍 Location: \${intake.city} (\${intake.venueType})\\n👥 Expected Guests: \~\${intake.guestCount}\\n💰 Target Allocation Range: \${vendor.estimatedPriceRangeINR}\`;  
  const body \= \`\\n\\n\${vendor.whatsappInquiryTemplate}\`;  
  const questions \=  
    vendor.vettingQuestions.length \> 0  
      ? \`\\n\\nKindly share availability and package details covering:\\n\${vendor.vettingQuestions  
          .map((q, i) \=\> \`\${i \+ 1}.\${q}\`)  
          .join('\\n')}\`  
      : '';

  return \`\${greeting}\${specs}\${body}\${questions}\\n\\nWarm regards\!\`;  
}

export function buildWhatsAppUrl(  
  intake: EventIntake,  
  vendor: VendorItem  
): string {  
  const fullMessage \= buildVendorWhatsAppMessage(intake, vendor);  
  return \`https\://wa.me/?text=\${encodeURIComponent(fullMessage)}\`;  
}

### **Smart Vendor Radar and Zero-Key Local Map (src/components/VendorRadarMap.tsx)**

To display nearby catering service centers, decoration service centers, photography service centers, and venues immediately after event setup without risking Google Cloud Maps SDK billing errors in sandboxed evaluation environments, VendorRadarMap.tsx pairs a dynamic Google Maps Search Embed iframe with the interactive vendor checklist matrix. The component maintains an activeCategory state ('Caterers' | 'Decorators' | 'Photographers' | 'Venues') and an editable locality search field initialized to state.intake.city. Whenever the host clicks a category filter pill, the iframe source updates deterministically:

TypeScript  
const activeMeta \=  
  MAP\_CATEGORIES.find((c) \=\> c.serviceCategory \=== activeCategory) ||  
  MAP\_CATEGORIES\[0\];  
const searchQuery \= \`\${activeMeta.queryTerm} near \${  
  customAreaSearch || state.intake.city  
}\`;  
const mapEmbedUrl \= \`https\://www\.google.com/maps?q=\${encodeURIComponent(  
  searchQuery  
)}\&output=embed\`;

Next to the live map, each vendor card displays the fair price estimate in Indian Rupees, the three vetting questions, a button to launch the pre-filled WhatsApp inquiry via buildWhatsAppUrl(), and inline fields to pin a discovered local business (pinnedVendorName) along with its quoted price (quotedPriceINR). Saving a vendor quote automatically synchronizes with the actualSpentINR property of the matching budget category in App.tsx.

### **Regional Feast and Theme Studio (src/components/FeastAndThemeStudio.tsx)**

This studio connects regional culinary identity directly to per-plate catering mathematics. At the top of the module, interactive **Regional Culinary Vibe Cards** (*🥥 Southern Sambar & Sadhya*, *🫓 Northern Naan & Nawabi*, *🌶️ Deccan & Royal Nizami*, and *🍕 Global Fusion & Street*) allow the host to switch culinary triggers at any point. Selecting a new regional trigger invokes rebalanceWithSahayak() with the updated regionalVibe, rewriting the welcome drinks, live counters, main course specialties, breads, rice, and desserts to fit the exact perPlateBudgetINR limit. Directly below the menu, the studio renders three distinct ThemeConcept cards, each displaying four interactive hex color swatches (style={{ backgroundColor: hex }}), decor focal points, guest engagement games, and a one-click copy button for the customized digital invitation text.
